title: On the Geometry of Separation in Finite Gaussian Mixtures
summary: We study an open problem of understanding the effects of the minimum component separation on the convergence rates of parameter estimation in finite Gaussian mixtures. We address this by developing a unified geometric framework based on novel Hellinger lower bounds that directly relate discrepancies between mixture densities directly to Wasserstein distances between their underlying mixing measures, with explicit dependence on both the minimum separation and the minimum weight.
